Claim 26 (Currently amended): A non-transitory machine readable medium storing a program which when executed by at least one processing unit analyzes a document, the program comprising sets of instructions for: receiving a document that comprises a plurality of primitive graphic elements defined separately within the document, the document having a drawing order that indicates the order in which the primitive graphic elements are drawn when the document is displayed; calculating a first value for a first primitive graphic element and a second primitive graphic element that is subsequent to the first in the drawing order, wherein the first value is based on __spatial proximity and relative positioning__ of the first and second primitive graphic elements; and based on the comparison of the first value to other values calculated for additional primitive graphic elements that are subsequent in the drawing order, defining a single structural graphic element within the document from the first and second primitive graphic elements __only when the first value satisfies a predetermined threshold indicating the first and second primitive graphic elements are intended to form a unified visual structure__.

Claim 27 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 26, wherein the first value is __derived from a combination of size and spatial relationship__ value.

Claim 28 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 26, wherein the first value represents __a normalized measure of spatial proximity combined with__ a size of a smallest bounding box that encompasses the first and second primitive graphic elements.

Claim 31 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 26, wherein the set of instructions for calculating comprises a set of instructions for calculating a different value for each pair of primitive graphic elements subsequent in the drawing order, wherein the set of instructions for defining the single structural graphic element comprises sets of instructions for: using the calculated values for pairs of primitive graphic elements to identify clusters of primitive graphic elements as candidates for joining as compound graphic elements __based on a determination that the primitive graphic elements share a common visual purpose__; and identifying sequences of primitive graphic elements within a cluster whose bounding boxes intersect __and whose spatial relationships indicate intentional grouping__; and joining the sequences as single graphic elements.

Claim 32 (Currently amended): A non-transitory machine readable medium storing a program which when executed by at least one processing unit analyzes a document, the program comprising sets of instructions for: receiving a document that comprises a plurality of primitive graphic elements defined separately within the document; based on values calculated for pairs of primitive graphic elements __that reflect spatial proximity and visual alignment__, defining a set of successive primitive graphic elements as a candidate compound graphic element; using bounds of the primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements within the set __based on contiguity and visual coherence__; and defining each particular subset having more than one primitive graphic element as a single structural graphic element within the document, the structure graphic element comprising the primitive graphic elements in the particular subset.

Claim 33 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 32, wherein the set of instructions for defining the set of successive primitive graphic elements comprises performing cluster analysis on the calculated values __to identify groups of primitive graphic elements that exhibit visual coherence and intentional spatial arrangement__.

Claim 34 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 32, wherein the set of instructions for using bounds of the primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements comprises sets of instructions for: selecting a first graphic element in the cluster and assigning the graphic element to a new sub-cluster; assigning a second graphic element in the cluster to the sub-cluster when a bounding box of the second graphic element overlaps a bounding box of the sub-cluster __and the second graphic element is visually aligned with the first graphic element__.

Claim 35 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 34, wherein the set of instructions for using bounds of the primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements further comprises a set of instructions for assigning a third graphic element to a second sub-cluster when a bounding box of the third graphic element does not overlap the bounding box of the sub-cluster __and the third graphic element exhibits visual characteristics distinct from the first sub-cluster__.

Claim 36 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 34, wherein the bounding box of the sub-cluster is __calculated as__ an intersection of the bounding boxes of all primitive graphic elements already in the sub-cluster __to define the spatial extent of the unified visual structure__.
